findings.finding: Mixed SOME/NO terms under Boolean congruence require a compositional mixed calculus, beyond separate relation nonemptiness propositions and pure Formula derivations. Bind final mixed soundness obligations and concrete witness in two clean exact-proposition builds.
findings.resolution: MixedFormula, substitution semantics, MixedDerivation and mixed_sound cover Boolean rule instances, Boolean congruence, and SOME/NO relation congruence. EG19/EG20 register the exact propositions. NOT constants are explicit Rule constructors with soundness cases.

findings.finding: Certificate checker must enforce exact atom payload/sort membership in fixed inventory, bounded term depth before recursive operations, and explicit output/certificate exhaustion semantics. Parent reports these precision fixes in progress.
findings.resolution: Inventory membership is bound to trusted adapter input, term/proof depths are explicitly capped at 128, and OUTPUT_LIMIT plus honest incomplete/unavailable behavior is specified.

findings.finding: Current EG15/16/17 declarations are universally quantified witnesses, but observed Lean witnesses instantiate concrete Fin 2/Fin 1 terms. Exact-proposition audit must bind actual intended concrete statements before gate approval.
findings.resolution: EG15/16/17 now state the concrete Fin 2/Fin 1 witnesses present in Lean.

findings.finding: Matcher operates modulo eclass equality while RULE certificates require concrete syntactic instantiation. For AND(a,b) where a=b is certified, repeated-variable idempotence requires child-congruence conversion to AND(a,a) before RULE or an equivalent explicit derivation. UF membership is not a certificate premise. Test this case, multi-level collision rebuild, historical endpoints after path compression, and forged equality without a derivation.
findings.resolution: Revision 2 checker explicitly requires concrete substitution and congruence; acceptance explicitly includes certified AND(a,b) repeated-variable regression.

findings.finding: Cycles and distributive expansion can exhaust matches/proofs before node budget; extraction must maintain finite positive-cost witnesses and root derivation, never serialize class cycles. Test cyclic x=AND(x,TRUE), duplicate unsuccessful matches, capped rebuilding, checked extraction during incomplete saturation, and proof replay cancellation.

Graph.justified assumes every class equality has derivation; extraction_sound follows this premise and does not establish actual Java union-find/rebuild/extractor correctness. Runtime full-schema mapping and fixed context/root binding remain trusted adapters. UI must preserve this distinction and solver analysis of original source.

commercialization.basis: Inherited contract and local baseline inventory, not independent legal clearance. Stage expressly disables commercial release, publication, dataset ingestion and external dependencies for egraph implementation.
commercialization.cost_limits: One-second egraph and ten-second worker limits are proposed operational ceilings, not measured latency, throughput, support cost, or margin evidence. Sixteen islands and per-island certificate limits require the global output cap and cooperative checks across proof construction/replay; external process deadline remains necessary.
commercialization.rights: Original Java implementation avoids introducing an external egraph library license. Existing exact Alloy/component redistribution and corpus rights remain release gates; no legal conclusion or license clearance is made.
commercialization.later_business_gate: Measure solver/egraph CPU and memory, failure rates, support effort and customer task benefit before commercial claims; no market or revenue estimates supported.

conditional_final_verdict: Revision 2 design and formal contract accepted for local implementation. Root must independently require successful two-clean-build exact-proposition audit for these frozen hashes before production edits. This review does not assert that running build gate has passed. Runtime tests, connected-browser UX acceptance and commercial release gates remain separate.
